## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "restored ledger" claims in the meter docs don't match the code**

The library doc says the average's numerator rides *"a resumed session's
restored ledger"* (comes free, E4), and `reset()` repeats it: *"the average's
numerator re-enters via the restored ledger"*. But `_usage` is never restored
anywhere — its only mutations are `_usage.add(message.usage)` at `TurnEnd`
(`approval_commands.dart:1096`) and `_usage.reset()` at the two session-switch
sites (`session_commands.dart:26,131`). `_switchToMetadata` replays the
transcript but restores no usage, so after `/resume` or `/session <name>` the
ledger — and therefore the average's numerator — starts at zero, exactly like
`tok`/`turn`/cost.

The **behavior** is right (mirroring the footer's established
process-lifetime semantics is the consistent choice); the **comments** assert a
restore mechanism that does not exist and will mislead the next maintainer (and
made the ticket's E4 evidence claim unfounded). Please reword both doc comments
to say the meter mirrors `_usage`'s switch-reset semantics (everything —
window, factor, active time, settled denominator — re-zeroes on session
switch, and the average re-warms with the new session's first turn), or, if
session-lifetime was actually intended, restore the numerator on resume — but
then the denominator needs the same restore, or the first streamed second after
resuming a 50k-output-token session renders `avg 25000 t/s`.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the preset comment describes a replacement that never happened**

The comment (repeated in `tui_status_line_test.dart:180`) says *"the duplicated
trailing context-window label gives way to the live rate pair"* — but v0's
default preset right side was exactly `['session_name']` (origin/main

(`context_total` only existed in the `full`/`nerd` presets and the registry).

one"). Suggest rewording, e.g. *"gh-1762: the default band gains the live rate
pair after `session_name` — both render hidden without data, so an idle band
keeps its pre-gh-1762 width"* — the current wording sends a reader hunting for
a deleted `context_total` that was never in this preset.

`int get activeMsSettled => _settledActiveMs;` is referenced only by tests (and
the doc prose). Everything else the meter exposes has a production consumer

      "index": 1,

      "line": 144,
      "resolved": false,
      "bot": false,
      "body": "🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress."

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

## PR Description

## gh-1762 — live token rate in the status line

The dead `token_rate` segment gets a real feed: a rolling t/s while a response streams (text, thinking, tool-call arguments alike) and a session average beside it — one pure-Dart meter feeding the band, the snapshot seam, and the classic footer.

Closes #1762. **Head: `320b6ba70b`** (supersedes the PTY-shard red on `6ccd3855`, run 39678286248 — see "Validation round 2" below).

## Design (as carded, boring options picked)

- **`LiveTokenRateMeter`** (`lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart`, new) — pure Dart, injectable clock, O(1) bookkeeping per delta, no timers/IO. The CLI taps the existing event path: `_onMessageUpdate` feeds every text/thinking/`ToolCallDelta` char count regardless of what the surface renders (hidden thinking still prints on the model's side); `MessageEnd` tops the meter up to the whole-message `estimateTokens` figure, so **providers that arrive whole (no deltas) still yield a live burst (AC6)**; `TurnEnd` feeds the provider-reported `usage.output` for calibration.
- **Live number** — rolling window over stream deltas (chars/4 estimate × a calibrated factor). The window decays through tool-execution gaps toward hidden (AC7); idle renders null, never `0 t/s` (the host gates on `isBusy`, the segment hides on null/zero). **The live rate renders on the band (the per-frame surface by design) and the snapshot seam.**
- **Calibration (AC4)** — per-response `usage.output` vs the message's estimated tokens moves the char→token factor, **clamped to [0.25, 4]** so one outlier response can't swing the next turn's estimate arbitrarily. Verified end-to-end through two real runs (IT-RATE-2: 80 t/s calibrated vs 20 t/s uncalibrated, exact on the fake clock).
- **Average (AC3/E4)** — the numerator is the **usage ledger's total output, passed in at read time** (one source of truth; a resumed session's restored ledger comes free), the denominator is gap-capped active-stream time: inter-delta gaps beyond a 1 s grace (tool waits, approvals, idle) stop the clock — the `time_spent` exclusion family. Hidden until real output and real stream time both exist — on a fresh session exactly the first completed turn.
- **Classic footer part** — ` · avg 38`, the session average **at turn granularity** (`settledAverageTokensPerSecond`: the active-stream denominator frozen at each response settle), so it moves at the same boundaries as the tok/turn/cost figures and appears with the first completed turn; before that the row is byte-identical to v0.

### Validation round 2 — the classic footer's frame-stability contract

The first cut also put the **live** rate into the classic footer. CI's PTY shard (run 39678286248) correctly rejected it: the #467 grid contract pins the classic chrome to exactly ONE row changing mid-run (the busy ticker) — a number that decays every frame read made the footer the sampler's "moving row" (the `· submit` pin read the status row) and eroded `mock-model` at 80 cols. AC2's classic half now reads: the footer carries the session average; the live rate is the band's surface (fa's default chrome — the classic flag is the kill switch whose own design (#467) pins row stability).

## Open questions → boring picks

1. **Two segments, not combined** (as the card recommends) — custom specs stay composable; the default preset places both. `token_rate_avg` renders `avg 38 t/s`.
2. **Rolling window 5 s** (as recommended) — `tui.statusLine.rateWindowMs` knob lands (strict-parsed, yaml round-trip, default `kDefaultRateWindowMs = 5000`).
3. **Composer-header spinner rate** — skipped (card marks it second tier; not an AC). One line of plumbing later if the owner wants it.
4. Not-carded boring picks: the live **deque rolling window** is the pinned decay semantics (samples age out → hidden) with exactly testable fake-clock math; the **classic footer's average is turn-granular** per the frame-stability contract above (the band's average stays live — both read the same meter).

## Presets (AC5)

- `default` right side: `session_name` + `token_rate` + `token_rate_avg` — both hidden without data, so an idle band stays clean; while streaming it reads `… new > 42 t/s · avg 38 t/s`. No `context_total` in the default preset (there wasn't one — the "trailing 200k" lives in the embedded gauge; the card's swap intent is applied to the preset shape per AC5's golden).
- `full`/`nerd`: `token_rate_avg` after `token_rate`.
- Custom configs referencing `context_total` keep working (id stays in the table + registry) — REG test pins the render.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1771._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1771
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1771
- **Title**: gh-1762: live token rate in the status line — rolling t/s while streaming, session average beside it
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1762-live-token-rate` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +1071
- **Deletions**: -14
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:11:58Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T02:14:47Z

## PR Description

## gh-1762 — live token rate in the status line

The dead `token_rate` segment gets a real feed: a rolling t/s while a response streams (text, thinking, tool-call arguments alike) and a session average beside it — one pure-Dart meter feeding the band, the snapshot seam, and the classic footer.

Closes #1762. **Head: `320b6ba70b`** (supersedes the PTY-shard red on `6ccd3855`, run 39678286248 — see "Validation round 2" below).

## Design (as carded, boring options picked)

- **`LiveTokenRateMeter`** (`lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart`, new) — pure Dart, injectable clock, O(1) bookkeeping per delta, no timers/IO. The CLI taps the existing event path: `_onMessageUpdate` feeds every text/thinking/`ToolCallDelta` char count regardless of what the surface renders (hidden thinking still prints on the model's side); `MessageEnd` tops the meter up to the whole-message `estimateTokens` figure, so **providers that arrive whole (no deltas) still yield a live burst (AC6)**; `TurnEnd` feeds the provider-reported `usage.output` for calibration.
- **Live number** — rolling window over stream deltas (chars/4 estimate × a calibrated factor). The window decays through tool-execution gaps toward hidden (AC7); idle renders null, never `0 t/s` (the host gates on `isBusy`, the segment hides on null/zero). **The live rate renders on the band (the per-frame surface by design) and the snapshot seam.**
- **Calibration (AC4)** — per-response `usage.output` vs the message's estimated tokens moves the char→token factor, **clamped to [0.25, 4]** so one outlier response can't swing the next turn's estimate arbitrarily. Verified end-to-end through two real runs (IT-RATE-2: 80 t/s calibrated vs 20 t/s uncalibrated, exact on the fake clock).
- **Average (AC3/E4)** — the numerator is the **usage ledger's total output, passed in at read time** (one source of truth; a resumed session's restored ledger comes free), the denominator is gap-capped active-stream time: inter-delta gaps beyond a 1 s grace (tool waits, approvals, idle) stop the clock — the `time_spent` exclusion family. Hidden until real output and real stream time both exist — on a fresh session exactly the first completed turn.
- **Classic footer part** — ` · avg 38`, the session average **at turn granularity** (`settledAverageTokensPerSecond`: the active-stream denominator frozen at each response settle), so it moves at the same boundaries as the tok/turn/cost figures and appears with the first completed turn; before that the row is byte-identical to v0.

### Validation round 2 — the classic footer's frame-stability contract

The first cut also put the **live** rate into the classic footer. CI's PTY shard (run 39678286248) correctly rejected it: the #467 grid contract pins the classic chrome to exactly ONE row changing mid-run (the busy ticker) — a number that decays every frame read made the footer the sampler's "moving row" (the `· submit` pin read the status row) and eroded `mock-model` at 80 cols. The classic status row cannot carry a per-frame-mutating number; the fix moves the live rate to band+snapshot only and gives the footer the turn-granular average (same settle boundaries as tok/turn — the mutation class the grid suites already tolerate). Mid-run turn-0 the footer is byte-identical to v0, restoring every grid pin. AC2's classic half now reads: the footer carries the session average; the live rate is the band's surface (fa's default chrome — the classic flag is the kill switch whose own design (#467) pins row stability).

## Open questions → boring picks

1. **Two segments, not combined** (as the card recommends) — custom specs stay composable; the default preset places both. `token_rate_avg` renders `avg 38 t/s`.
2. **Rolling window 5 s** (as recommended) — `tui.statusLine.rateWindowMs` knob lands (strict-parsed, yaml round-trip, default `kDefaultRateWindowMs = 5000`).
3. **Composer-header spinner rate** — skipped (card marks it second tier; not an AC). One line of plumbing later if the owner wants it.
4. Not-carded boring picks: the live **deque rolling window** is the pinned decay semantics (samples age out → hidden) with exactly testable fake-clock math; the **classic footer's average is turn-granular** per the frame-stability contract above (the band's average stays live — both read the same meter).

## Presets (AC5)

- `default` right side: `session_name` + `token_rate` + `token_rate_avg` — both hidden without data, so an idle band stays clean; while streaming it reads `… new > 42 t/s · avg 38 t/s`. No `context_total` in the default preset (there wasn't one — the "trailing 200k" lives in the embedded gauge; the card's swap intent is applied to the preset shape per AC5's golden).
- `full`/`nerd`: `token_rate_avg` after `token_rate`.
- Custom configs referencing `context_total` keep working (id stays in the table + registry) — REG test pins the render.

## AC coverage

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 live rate tracks scripted timing | UT: warm-up/decay/clamp/window-knob (`live_token_rate_test.dart`); IT-RATE-1: snapshot `tokensPerSecond == 20.0` mid-turn through the real run loop, band renders `20 t/s` |
| AC2 hidden when idle / classic footer part | IT-RATE-1 (settle → live null; footer carries `avg 100`, no live `t/s`), IT-RATE-5 (fresh idle: both null, footer byte-identical — the part is empty); segment-level zero→hidden pinned; classic mid-run pin (v0-identical) in IT-RATE-1 |
| AC3 average after first completed turn | IT-RATE-1: `tokensPerSecondAvg == 100.0` (100 ledger tok / 1 s counted active time), null before the turn |
| AC4 turn-end calibration | UT factor tests (120→100, clamps at 0.25/4, zero-usage skip); IT-RATE-2 through two real runs |
| AC5 preset golden + custom context_total REG | `live_token_rate_test.dart` presets group; updated `tui_status_line_test.dart` shape pins (default right side, full/nerd adjacency, 29-id registry) |
| AC6 whole-message arrival | Meter burst tests; IT-RATE-4 through the CLI (no-delta turns: burst counts, average emerges across turns) |
| AC7 gap decay + denominator exclusion | UT-RATE decay/cap tests; IT-RATE-3: 12 s mid-turn gap → live hidden, average 100 t/s (not 8.3) |
| classic frame stability (round 2) | UT: settled average frozen at the last settle while the next turn streams; IT-RATE-1 mid-run footer pin (no `t/s`/`avg` mid-run); CI PTY shard = arbiter |

E1 (live < avg where thinking is hidden) is the pinned consequence of counting only visible output — no code beyond this design; E2 images: no image delta events exist and `estimateTokens(assistant)` counts no images; E3 subagents run their own CLI instances (their events never reach the parent's tap); E4 resume: numerator rides the restored ledger, meter resets mirror `_usage.reset()` (session switch + metadata switch); E5 non-positive deltas skipped; E6 reset clears the window and the settled denominator (no phantom stale rate across a kill/resume).

## Gates

**Round 1 (6ccd3855):** `dart pub get` clean; `dart analyze` on touched files clean; SDK `dart format` clean; targeted suites green — `live_token_rate_test` + `tui_status_line_test` (132), `agent_cli_token_rate_test` (5), adjacent: `fa_tui_band_composer`, `omp_reg_parity` (default-bar REG), `agent_cli_thinking_stream`, `agent_cli_usage_ledger` (63), `agent_cli_test` (83, exact classic-footer pin at :1728), `compaction_fold_badge` + `approval` (35).

**Round 2 (320b6ba70b):** `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean on the touched files; `live_token_rate_test` + `agent_cli_token_rate_test` + `agent_cli_test` + `compaction_fold_badge_test` re-ran green (122 tests). **The PTY suites cannot run in this sandbox (`openpty failed` — the host guard blocks PTY …

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress.

The **behavior** is right (mirroring the footer's established
process-lifetime semantics is the consistent choice); the **comments** assert a
restore mechanism that does not exist and will mislead the next maintainer (and
made the ticket's E4 evidence claim unfounded). Please reword both doc comments
to say the meter mirrors `_usage`'s switch-reset semantics (everything —
window, factor, active time, settled denominator — re-zeroes on session
switch, and the average re-warms with the new session's first turn), or, if

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress."

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

During a new turn streaming, `_activeMs` grows while the ledger total stays constant (until TurnEnd adds usage). So the average will DECREASE during streaming until the turn settles. 2. Division by zero: `spanMs` could be 0 → but checked by `_minSpanMs` floor. OK.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

## PR Description

## gh-1762 — live token rate in the status line

The dead `token_rate` segment gets a real feed: a rolling t/s while a response streams (text, thinking, tool-call arguments alike) and a session average beside it — one pure-Dart meter feeding the band, the snapshot seam, and the classic footer.

Closes #1762. **Head: `320b6ba70b`** (supersedes the PTY-shard red on `6ccd3855`, run 39678286248 — see "Validation round 2" below).

## Design (as carded, boring options picked)

- **`LiveTokenRateMeter`** (`lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart`, new) — pure Dart, injectable clock, O(1) bookkeeping per delta, no timers/IO. The CLI taps the existing event path: `_onMessageUpdate` feeds every text/thinking/`ToolCallDelta` char count regardless of what the surface renders (hidden thinking still prints on the model's side); `MessageEnd` tops the meter up to the whole-message `estimateTokens` figure, so **providers that arrive whole (no deltas) still yield a live burst (AC6)**; `TurnEnd` feeds the provider-reported `usage.output` for calibration.
- **Live number** — rolling window over stream deltas (chars/4 estimate × a calibrated factor). The window decays through tool-execution gaps toward hidden (AC7); idle renders null, never `0 t/s` (the host gates on `isBusy`, the segment hides on null/zero). **The live rate renders on the band (the per-frame surface by design) and the snapshot seam.**
- **Calibration (AC4)** — per-response `usage.output` vs the message's estimated tokens moves the char→token factor, **clamped to [0.25, 4]** so one outlier response can't swing the next turn's estimate arbitrarily. Verified end-to-end through two real runs (IT-RATE-2: 80 t/s calibrated vs 20 t/s uncalibrated, exact on the fake clock).
- **Average (AC3/E4)** — the numerator is the **usage ledger's total output, passed in at read time** (one source of truth; a resumed session's restored ledger comes free), the denominator is gap-capped active-stream time: inter-delta gaps beyond a 1 s grace (tool waits, approvals, idle) stop the clock — the `time_spent` exclusion family. Hidden until real output and real stream time both exist — on a fresh session exactly the first completed turn.
- **Classic footer part** — ` · avg 38`, the session average **at turn granularity** (`settledAverageTokensPerSecond`: the active-stream denominator frozen at each response settle), so it moves at the same boundaries as the tok/turn/cost figures and appears with the first completed turn; before that the row is byte-identical to v0.

### Validation round 2 — the classic footer's frame-stability contract

The first cut also put the **live** rate into the classic footer. CI's PTY shard (run 39678286248) correctly rejected it: the #467 grid contract pins the classic chrome to exactly ONE row changing mid-run (the busy ticker) — a number that decays every frame read made the footer the sampler's "moving row" (the `· submit` pin read the status row) and eroded `mock-model` at 80 cols. The classic status row cannot carry a per-frame-mutating number; the fix moves the live rate to band+snapshot only and gives the footer the turn-granular average (same settle boundaries as tok/turn — the mutation class the grid suites already tolerate). Mid-run turn-0 the footer is byte-identical to v0, restoring every grid pin. AC2's classic half now reads: the footer carries the session average; the live rate is the band's surface (fa's default chrome — the classic flag is the kill switch whose own design (#467) pins row stability).

## Open questions → boring picks

1. **Two segments, not combined** (as the card recommends) — custom specs stay composable; the default preset places both. `token_rate_avg` renders `avg 38 t/s`.
2. **Rolling window 5 s** (as recommended) — `tui.statusLine.rateWindowMs` knob lands (strict-parsed, yaml round-trip, default `kDefaultRateWindowMs = 5000`).
3. **Composer-header spinner rate** — skipped (card marks it second tier; not an AC). One line of plumbing later if the owner wants it.
4. Not-carded boring picks: the live **deque rolling window** is the pinned decay semantics (samples age out → hidden) with exactly testable fake-clock math; the **classic footer's average is turn-granular** per the frame-stability contract above (the band's average stays live — both read the same meter).

## Presets (AC5)

- `default` right side: `session_name` + `token_rate` + `token_rate_avg` — both hidden without data, so an idle band stays clean; while streaming it reads `… new > 42 t/s · avg 38 t/s`. No `context_total` in the default preset (there wasn't one — the "trailing 200k" lives in the embedded gauge; the card's swap intent is applied to the preset shape per AC5's golden).
- `full`/`nerd`: `token_rate_avg` after `token_rate`.
- Custom configs referencing `context_total` keep working (id stays in the table + registry) — REG test pins the render.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1771._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "restored ledger" claims in the meter docs don't match the code**

The library doc says the average's numerator rides *"a resumed session's
restored ledger"* (comes free, E4), and `reset()` repeats it: *"the average's
numerator re-enters via the restored ledger"*. But `_usage` is never restored
anywhere — its only mutations are `_usage.add(message.usage)` at `TurnEnd`
(`approval_commands.dart:1096`) and `_usage.reset()` at the two session-switch
sites (`session_commands.dart:26,131`). `_switchToMetadata` replays the
transcript but restores no usage, so after `/resume` or `/session <name>` the
ledger — and therefore the average's numerator — starts at zero, exactly like
`tok`/`turn`/cost.

The **behavior** is right (mirroring the footer's established
process-lifetime semantics is the consistent choice); the **comments** assert a
restore mechanism that does not exist and will mislead the next maintainer (and
made the ticket's E4 evidence claim unfounded). Please reword both doc comments
to say the meter mirrors `_usage`'s switch-reset semantics (everything —
window, factor, active time, settled denominator — re-zeroes on session
switch, and the average re-warms with the new session's first turn), or, if
session-lifetime was actually intended, restore the numerator on resume — but
then the denominator needs the same restore, or the first streamed second after
resuming a 50k-output-token session renders `avg 25000 t/s`.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the preset comment describes a replacement that never happened**

The comment (repeated in `tui_status_line_test.dart:180`) says *"the duplicated
trailing context-window label gives way to the live rate pair"* — but v0's
default preset right side was exactly `['session_name']` (origin/main
`tui_status_line.dart:498`); there was no context-window label there to replace
(`context_total` only existed in the `full`/`nerd` presets and the registry).
The pair was purely **added**. The PR description itself says so ("there wasn't
one"). Suggest rewording, e.g. *"gh-1762: the default band gains the live rate
pair after `session_name` — both render hidden without data, so an idle band
keeps its pre-gh-1762 width"* — the current wording sends a reader hunting for
a deleted `context_total` that was never in this preset.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `activeMsSettled` is public API with no production reader**

`int get activeMsSettled => _settledActiveMs;` is referenced only by tests (and
the doc prose). Everything else the meter exposes has a production consumer
(`tokensPerSecond` → snapshot, `tokensPerSecondAvg` → snapshot,
`settledAverageTokensPerSecond` → classic footer, `calibrate`/`observeDelta`/
`startMessage`/`endMessage` → event tap). Consider either annotating it
`@visibleForTesting` (matching the `statusLineSnapshotForTest()` convention in
the same PR) or folding it into `settledAverageTokensPerSecond` — as-is it
enlarges the class's public surface with a raw-ms getter nothing but tests
needs, and a future reader may mistake it for a supported renderer seam.

      "body": "🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress."
