# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress.

restored ledger"* (comes free, E4), and `reset()` repeats it: *"the average's
numerator re-enters via the restored ledger"*. But `_usage` is never restored

(`approval_commands.dart:1096`) and `_usage.reset()` at the two session-switch
sites (`session_commands.dart:26,131`). `_switchToMetadata` replays the
transcript but restores no usage, so after `/resume` or `/session <name>` the
ledger — and therefore the average's numerator — starts at zero, exactly like
`tok`/`turn`/cost.

The **behavior** is right (mirroring the footer's established
process-lifetime semantics is the consistent choice); the **comments** assert a
restore mechanism that does not exist and will mislead the next maintainer (and
made the ticket's E4 evidence claim unfounded). Please reword both doc comments
to say the meter mirrors `_usage`'s switch-reset semantics (everything —
window, factor, active time, settled denominator — re-zeroes on session
switch, and the average re-warms with the new session's first turn), or, if
session-lifetime was actually intended, restore the numerator on resume — but
then the denominator needs the same restore, or the first streamed second after
resuming a 50k-output-token session renders `avg 25000 t/s`.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the preset comment describes a replacement that never happened**

The comment (repeated in `tui_status_line_test.dart:180`) says *"the duplicated

`int get activeMsSettled => _settledActiveMs;` is referenced only by tests (and

- **Live number** — rolling window over stream deltas (chars/4 estimate × a calibrated factor). The window decays through tool-execution gaps toward hidden (AC7); idle renders null, never `0 t/s` (the host gates on `isBusy`, the segment hides on null/zero). **The live rate renders on the band (the per-frame surface by design) and the snapshot seam.**
- **Calibration (AC4)** — per-response `usage.output` vs the message's estimated tokens moves the char→token factor, **clamped to [0.25, 4]** so one outlier response can't swing the next turn's estimate arbitrarily. - **Average (AC3/E4)** — the numerator is the **usage ledger's total output, passed in at read time** (one source of truth; a resumed session's restored ledger comes free), the denominator is gap-capped active-stream time: inter-delta gaps beyond a 1 s grace (tool waits, approvals, idle) stop the clock — the `time_spent` exclusion family. - **Classic footer part** — ` · avg 38`, the session average **at turn granularity** (`settledAverageTokensPerSecond`: the active-stream denominator frozen at each response settle), so it moves at the same boundaries as the tok/turn/cost figures and appears with the first completed turn; before that the row is byte-identical to v0.

t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress."

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

The reset() doc says "the meter re-warms with the session's own ledger — the CLI resets both together". No more "restored ledger comes free" claims. ✓

One subtle behavior in `calibrate`: `_settledActiveMs = _activeMs;` — the settle freezes the active time. But note `calibrate` is called at TurnEnd after `_usage.add(message.usage)`. Good.

Potential issues to consider:

1. `tokensPerSecondAvg` uses `_activeMs` (live denominator), while the snapshot reads `tokensPerSecondAvg(total.output)` — the band's average is live. During a new turn streaming, `_activeMs` grows while the ledger total stays constant (until TurnEnd adds usage). So the average will DECREASE during streaming until the turn settles. That's by design ("band's average stays live (per-frame by design)").

2. Division by zero: `spanMs` could be 0 → but checked by `_minSpanMs` floor. OK.

3. `_prune` uses `<=` cutoff; window boundary inclusive. Fine.

4. In `tokensPerSecond`, note the pruning at read time: if the read happens without new deltas (idle decay), it prunes and hides. Good.

5. `observeDelta` maps chars/4 * factor. `calibrate` multiplies `_factor * outputTokens / _messageTokens`. `_messageTokens` is the sum of the per-message estimated tokens (raw, before factor? No — `_count` already applies the factor: `_messageTokens += tokens` where tokens = chars/4*factor. So `_messageTokens` is factor-adjusted estimate. If the true relation is tokens_true = chars/4 * factor_true, and message estimated with factor f: _messageTokens = chars/4*f. outputTokens is real. New factor = f * outputTokens / (chars/4 * f) = outputTokens / (chars/4). Correct — the factor converges to outputTokens/(chars/4). Good math.

7. Edge: `calibrate` sets `_messageTokens = 0` — so between calibrate and next startMessage, a stray endMessage would compute topUp = estimated - 0 = full message again. But endMessage is only called at message end, calibrate at turn end. If a turn has multiple assistant messages: startMessage, deltas, endMessage(est1); startMessage, deltas, endMessage(est2); turn end → calibrate(output). _messageTokens accumulates est1+est2 (both messages), and calibrate uses the total.  _onAssistantMessageEnd(message);
}
``

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1771._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).

  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is

  dropped entirely leaves a one-line tombstone naming its path instead of
  vanishing; and the user gets a dim boot line per truncated/dropped file
  (CLI line mode prints directly, TUI re-prints after the banner, the app
  logs through its AppLog boot-notice seam). New `projectContext:` config
  section: `maxBytes` (default 32768) — `0` disables the section entirely
  and reads no files (fast boot); unknown keys are tolerated with a note.
  Leaf-first allocation is unchanged.

- fix(gh-1757): the Android build no longer re-enters the sdkmanager
  download roulette for CMake. v1.0.619's `build-android` leg died at
  `:jni:configureCMakeDebug[arm64-v8a]` — the `:jni` module (transitive
  `jni` package via path_provider_android) wires externalNativeBuild.cmake
  with no version, so AGP auto-installed its default `cmake;3.22.1`
  mid-configuration and one corrupt archive ("Archive is not a ZIP
  archive") red'd the leg, the aggregate Quality gate, and the
  Advance-vpinned-marker job. The gh-1655 pre-install action now also
  pre-installs `cmake;3.22.1` with bounded retry + idempotent skip (same
  hardening the NDK path already carries); the guard test pins the new
  AC6 assertions and the AGP-version coupling (AC7).
- feat(#1750): per-model image caps — the outbound request never carries

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "restored ledger" claims in the meter docs don't match the code**

The library doc says the average's numerator rides *"a resumed session's
restored ledger"* (comes free, E4), and `reset()` repeats it: *"the average's
numerator re-enters via the restored ledger"*. But `_usage` is never restored
anywhere — its only mutations are `_usage.add(message.usage)` at `TurnEnd`

sites (`session_commands.dart:26,131`). `_switchToMetadata` replays the
transcript but restores no usage, so after `/resume` or `/session <name>` the
ledger — and therefore the average's numerator — starts at zero, exactly like
`tok`/`turn`/cost.

The **behavior** is right (mirroring the footer's established
process-lifetime semantics is the consistent choice); the **comments** assert a
restore mechanism that does not exist and will mislead the next maintainer (and
made the ticket's E4 evidence claim unfounded). Please reword both doc comments
to say the meter mirrors `_usage`'s switch-reset semantics (everything —
window, factor, active time, settled denominator — re-zeroes on session
switch, and the average re-warms with the new session's first turn), or, if
session-lifetime was actually intended, restore the numerator on resume — but
then the denominator needs the same restore, or the first streamed second after
resuming a 50k-output-token session renders `avg 25000 t/s`.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the preset comment describes a replacement that never happened**

The comment (repeated in `tui_status_line_test.dart:180`) says *"the duplicated
trailing context-window label gives way to the live rate pair"* — but v0's
default preset right side was exactly `['session_name']` (origin/main

(`context_total` only existed in the `full`/`nerd` presets and the registry).
The pair was purely **added**. The PR description itself says so ("there wasn't
one"). Suggest rewording, e.g. *"gh-1762: the default band gains the live rate
pair after `session_name` — both render hidden without data, so an idle band
keeps its pre-gh-1762 width"* — the current wording sends a reader hunting for
a deleted `context_total` that was never in this preset.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `activeMsSettled` is public API with no production reader**

`int get activeMsSettled => _settledActiveMs;` is referenced only by tests (and
the doc prose). Everything else the meter exposes has a production consumer
(`tokensPerSecond` → snapshot, `tokensPerSecondAvg` → snapshot,
`settledAverageTokensPerSecond` → classic footer, `calibrate`/`observeDelta`/

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

During a new turn streaming, `_activeMs` grows while the ledger total stays constant (until TurnEnd adds usage). So the average will DECREASE during streaming until the turn settles. That's by design ("band's average stays live (per-frame by design)").

2. Division by zero: `spanMs` could be 0 → but checked by `_minSpanMs` floor. OK.

If the true relation is tokens_true = chars/4 * factor_true, and message estimated with factor f: _messageTokens = chars/4*f. outputTokens is real. New factor = f * outputTokens / (chars/4 * f) = outputTokens / (chars/4). Correct — the factor converges to outputTokens/(chars/4). Good math.

If a turn has multiple assistant messages: startMessage, deltas, endMessage(est1); startMessage, deltas, endMessage(est2); turn end → calibrate(output). _messageTokens accumulates est1+est2 (both messages), and calibrate uses the total. }
``

a) `LiveTokenRateMeter` clamps and arithmetic edge: `_factor` used in `observeDelta` — `chars / _charsPerToken * _factor` — chars is int, `/` is double division. Fine.

b) `endMessage(int estimatedTokens)` — estimateTokens returns int? Let me check the signature of estimateTokens.

d) The band average during a fresh turn streams: `_activeMs` grows; numerator (ledger) unchanged → average decays. Design choice, documented.

e) `_statusRatePart()` — classic footer, reads `settledAverageTokensPerSecond(_usage.total.output)` — the numerator here is the ledger total, which grows at TurnEnd BEFORE `calibrate` updates `_settledActiveMs`. Both happen synchronously inside the same `onTurnEnd` callback, and the footer is read per frame — no intermediate frame can observe numerator-new/denominator-old because callbacks are synchronous. ✓

f) What about `_usage.add(message.usage)` when `message.usage.output` is 0 (some providers don't report usage at turn end)? Then ledger numerator doesn't move; calibrate(0) skips factor update but still settles `_settledActiveMs = _activeMs`. Footer unchanged (numerator same). Average unchanged numerator. Fine.

n) Performance: `_prune` amortized O(1) per delta; `tokensPerSecond` O(1) amortized per read (queue removals). `observeDelta` per delta event — negligible. ✓

o) Backward compat: `StatusLineSnapshot` additive optional field — the flutter app compiles. The band composer default preset changed shape — the omp parity test pins the default BAR RENDER: the reference file `02_status_bar_default.txt` — how does it compare? If the parity test compares fa's default bar against the omp REFERENCE text, adding segments would change the render... but round 1 ran it green. r) The meter's `windowMs` could be absurdly large via config (e.g. 10^12 ms) — memory growth: samples accumulate for windowMs duration — a user setting rateWindowMs: 999 would accumulate every delta sample for ~31 years → unbounded memory. Strict parse only requires positive int. Edge case: is this worth flaging? The knob is a status-line nicety; a huge value also makes the live rate meaningless. A sane upper bound (e.g. clamp to some max) would be defensive. Low severity — SUGESTION. Hmm, but honestly a user could shoot their own foot; the config knob is documented as a window in ms. ## Unreleased

- feat(#1761): the 32KB project-context budget never cuts silently again.
  A file truncated to its head excerpt now carries an extended
  `<!-- From: path — N bytes, only the first M shown -->` marker plus an
  explicit MUST-read-the-full-file instruction (offset/limit/ranges,
  prompt copy in `prompts/context/project_context_read_full.md`); a file
  dropped entirely leaves a one-line tombstone naming its path instead of
  vanishing; and the user gets a dim boot line per truncated/dropped file
  (CLI line mode prints directly, TUI re-prints after the banner, the app
  logs through its AppLog boot-notice seam). New `projectContext:` config
  section: `maxBytes` (default 32768) — `0` disables the section entirely
  and reads no files (fast boot); unknown keys are tolerated with a note.
  Leaf-first allocation is unchanged.

- fix(gh-1757): the Android build no longer re-enters the sdkmanager
  download roulette for CMake. v1.0.619's `build-android` leg died at
  `:jni:configureCMakeDebug[arm64-v8a]` — the `:jni` module (transitive
  `jni` package via path_provider_android) wires externalNativeBuild.cmake
  with no version, so AGP auto-installed its default `cmake;3.22.1`
  mid-configuration and one corrupt archive ("Archive is not a ZIP
  archive") red'd the leg, the aggregate Quality gate, and the
  Advance-vpinned-marker job. The gh-1655 pre-install action now also
  pre-installs `cmake;3.22.1` with bounded retry + idempotent skip (same
  hardening the NDK path already carries); the guard test pins the new
  AC6 assertions and the AGP-version coupling (AC7).
- feat(#1750): per-model image caps — the outbound request never carries

The repo's CHANGELOG.md convention: `## Unreleased` with entries per feature PR (e.g. feat(#1761), fix(gh-1757), feat(#1750)). gh-1762 (a user-visible feature: live token rate in the status line) has NO Unreleased entry. Comparable feature PRs (#1761, #1750) added entries. That's a legitimate finding — a repo-convention deviation (IMPORTANT or SUGESTION?). The review guidelines say "Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description". The PR description doesn't mention CHANGELOG. It's a real repo-convention gap but doesn't block merge — I'd rate it ⚠️ IMPORTANT? Hmm. Let me gauge: the machine's rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug/red CI/scope violation/security; IMPORTANT = real maintainability debt worth fixing. A missing changelog line is a small convention miss — previous review rounds (round 1) did NOT flag it. Given this is a re-review round and the missing changelog entry is user-visible-feature convention, I'd file it as 💡 SUGESTION... but let me check whether recent feature PRs consistently did it. #1761, #1757, #1750 all have entries. Consistent pattern → a missing entry is a deviation. I'll file SUGESTION (it's release bookeeping; the release fold process exists, and "curated-only" says add new lines under Unreleased — it's expected but not blocking). Actually — considering "IMPORTANT = real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped" vs "SUGESTION = optional improvement/style". A missing changelog entry for a user-visible feature is arguably IMPORTANT-ish in this repo since every sibling feature has one. But severity guidance says when in doubt start one level higher... "When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible." Risk here is negligible (release tooling folds entries; missing line just loses a changelog note). Hmm. I'll file it as 💡 SUGESTION to avoid arming a rework round for a changelog line — no wait. Let me be careful: the verdict rules say APPROVE if no BLOCKING, regardless of IMPORTANT/SUGESTION counts. IMPORTANT findings don't force REQUEST_CHANGES. So classifying as IMPORTANT is safe for the verdict (still APPROVE). The machine parses only blocking counts for rework. So I can honestly file: missing CHANGELOG entry = ⚠️ IMPORTANT (deviation from established per-PR convention for a user-visible feature), plus the leftover test comment = 💡 SUGESTION.

Wait — but hold on. Is the CHANGELOG entry requirement documented anywhere binding? AGENTS.md may mention it. Let me grep AGENTS.md for changelog guidance.

Also, let me do one more pass for any real issues I might have missed:

1. The `_minSpanMs` floor interplay with the window: `tokensPerSecond` requires spanMs = now - samples.first.tMs ≥ 250. After a decay gap (e.g. a 3s pause mid-response, window NOT fully empty — sample at t=4.5s, now=5.5s...), samples remain (within 5s window), span ≥ 250 — rate computed from remaining samples. Fine.

2. What about `tokensPerSecond` when the FIRST sample of the window is old but there are new samples: span anchored on oldest — standard rolling window. OK.

3. `observeDelta` during idle-wake turns: `_hasActivity` persists across turns; activeMs accrues gap-capped (≤1s grace) between turns — a new turn 30s later adds 1s (grace cap) to the denominator. Hmm — is that right? The design: "inter-delta gaps beyond a 1s grace (tool waits, approvals, idle) stop the clock". "Stop the clock" = contribute 0? NO — the code adds the GRACE CAP (1s) for longer gaps: `_activeMs += gap <= 0 ? 0 : (gap > _gapGraceMs ? _gapGraceMs : gap)`. So a 30s idle gap adds 1s, not 0. The doc says "gaps longer than the grace window are tool waits, approvals, or idle and stop the clock". "Stop the clock" implies 0, but the code adds the 1s cap. Contradiction? Let me re-read:

``
/// Streaming gaps longer than this stop the average's clock: real print
/// bursts arrive within hundreds of ms of each other; longer silences are
/// tool execution, approvals, or idle (AC7).
const int _gapGraceMs = 100;
``

and `_count`: `_activeMs += gap <= 0 ? 0 : (gap > _gapGraceMs ? _gapGraceMs : gap)`.

So a gap longer than grace contributes exactly `_gapGraceMs` (1s), not 0. "Stops the clock" is loose wording — the clock runs for at most the grace period then stops. Is this behavior sensible? The PR description says: "the denominator is gap-capped active-stream time: inter-delta gaps beyond a 1 s grace (tool waits, approvals, idle) stop the clock — the time_spent exclusion family". "Gap-capped" = capped at the grace. So capped-at-1s IS the documented design ("gap-capped"). The UT-RATE-6 pins: 12s gap counted as the 1s grace cap. Consistent with design. OK, not a bug.

But consider the average across a session with many tool-heavy turns: each inter-turn gap adds ≤1s. E.g., 10 turns each with a 60s tool wait between: denominator = sum of real print time + 10s of caps. The average stays meaningful-ish. Design accepted by previous round. Fine.

4. Cross-turn within one response? N/A.

5. `tokensPerSecondAvg` when `total.output` comes from the ledger: ledger includes ONLY live turns (resumed sessions start at 0) — denominator `_activeMs` also starts at 0 (reset). Consistent numerator/denominator across resume — both process-lifetime. ✓ (fixed doc matches).

6. The band average could differ from the footer average mid-turn (live vs settled) — documented. OK.

7. One more: `statusLineSnapshotForTest()` returns `_statusLineSnapshot()` — but the band uses `statusSnapshot: config.tuiClassic ? null : _statusLineSnapshot` — a tear-off. Fine.

8. `endMessage` — `_messageTokens` update condition: `if (estimatedTokens > _messageTokens) _messageTokens = estimatedTokens.toDouble();` — when streamed deltas overcounted (est < deltas), keep the delta count for calibration (conservative). ✓.

9. Meter and `_assistantPrefixPrinted` — nothing.

10. Multiple assistant messages per turn, calibrate at turn end sees combined `_messageTokens` — matches combined usage.output. ✓

11. Hmm, one more potential issue: `_meter.calibrate(message.usage.output)` is called in `onTurnEnd` — but `onTurnEnd` also fires for turns that end with an ERROR or cancellation? If a turn is cancelled mid-stream, TurnEndEvent may still fire with partial usage. Calibration with partial output — clamped, bounded. Fine.

12. Now, `session_commands.dart` — the two reset sites mirror `_usage.reset()`. Any other place calling `_meter` reset needed? `/clear`? Let me grep for a clear command that resets usage... `grep -n "clear" lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart`. The earlier grep showed only 2 `_usage.reset()` sites in lib/, and both are mirrored. ✓

13. Also — the round-2 author note says "meter resets mirror `_usage.reset()` (session switch + metadata switch)". ✓ verified.

14. `kStatusLineSegmentIds` order — 'token_rate_avg' after 'token_rate'; registry map insertion. ✓

15. Is there a schema file (schema/*.ts) that pins segment ids for the web client? The test comment says "the omp 27 segment ids (`schema.ts` `STATUS_LINE_SEGMENT_IDS`) plus fa's extensions". The web client (site/ or browser_ext/?) uses its own schema. fa's additions (timer, token_rate_avg) are fa-extensions — omp schema unchanged. Custom configs referencing unknown ids: "Ids with no fa counterpart data ... stay valid and render hidden". Fine.

16. Test quality: UTs use exact fake-clock math, IT through the real run loop with gates — solid, not string-only brittle. The `renderStatusLine` band render assertions use `contains`. Fine.

17. Now the leftover: line 180-182 comment. That's an added line in the diff → valid inline target.

18. Anything else in the exhaustive pass? Let me check the `full` preset list once more — in the diff, full has 'token_rate_avg' after 'token_rate' ✓; nerd likewise ✓.

19. `formatTokenRate` is now public in tui_status_line.dart and imported (show) into agent_cli.dart. `agent_cli.dart` is at 2529 lines < 280 gate ✓. tui_status_line.dart 2008 < 280 ✓.

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/live_token_rate_meter.dart` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the live rate spikes to absurd values at the start of every response**

`LiveTokenRateMeter.tokensPerSecond` computes the rate as
`windowTokens * 1000 / (now - _samples.first.tMs)` — the span is anchored on the
oldest sample **in the window**, with no minimum span. On the first frames of a
stream the window holds exactly one burst, so the formula degenerates to
`burst / time-since-that-burst`, and the band re-renders that number every
~16 ms (the composer's `_outputFlushInterval`).

Simulating the meter's exact math on a realistic stream (10-tok deltas every
200 ms = a true **50 t/s**, band reads every 16 ms):

```text
t= 16 ms  ->  625.0 t/s     <- 12.5× the true rate
t= 32 ms  ->  312.5 t/s
t= 48 ms  ->  208.3 t/s
t= 96 ms  ->  104.2 t/s
t=192 ms  ->   52.1 t/s     <- converges only after ~200 ms
```

The spike magnitude is independent of the true rate — it is
`first-burst tokens / 16 ms`:

- a 40-char first delta (10 tok) flashes **625 t/s**;
- a 500-token whole-message arrival (AC6 path) flashes **31,250 t/s** for the
  frames before the run settles;
- every subsequent delta re-spikes the number (the saw-tooth at t=208, 416, …
  above), so the value is visibly unstable even after the initial decay.

This violates the meter's own contract, stated in this same file: *"the number
reflects PRINT speed"* and *"hidden, never `0 t/s` (AC2, AC7)"* — a 625 t/s
flash is neither print speed nor hidden, and it renders on the default preset's
band (`… new > 625 t/s · avg …`) at the start of every response. Users will read
it as a glitch. No existing test covers the first-frames window (IT-RATE-1
samples at +500 ms, after the spike has decayed), so the suites stay green while
every real session sees it.

**Suggested fix** (one line, keeps the "hidden rather than bogus" contract):

```dart
double? get tokensPerSecond {
  final nowMs = _now().millisecondsSinceEpoch;
  _prune(nowMs);
  if (_samples.isEmpty) return null;
  final spanMs = nowMs - _samples.first.tMs;
  // A span below one inter-delta interval is not yet a rate — hide instead
  // of reporting burst/span (the first frames of every stream would
  // otherwise read burst/16ms, e.g. 625 t/s for a 10-tok burst at 50 t/s).
  if (spanMs < kMinRateSpanMs) return null; // e.g. const kMinRateSpanMs = 250;
  return _windowTokens * 1000 / spanMs;
}
```

(An alternative that keeps the number visible from the first frame: divide by
`max(spanMs, windowMsAfterFirstSample)` with a nominal first-interval — but the
hide-until-meaningful variant matches the segment's existing "null, never a
placeholder" semantics and needs no new state.)

Please also add a UT pinning the first-frames behavior (e.g. one delta at t0,
read at t0+16 must be hidden or ≤ a sane bound), so the artifact cannot
regress.

---

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "restored ledger" claims in the meter docs don't match the code**

The library doc says the average's numerator rides *"a resumed session's
restored ledger"* (comes free, E4), and `reset()` repeats it: *"the average's
numerator re-enters via the restored ledger"*. But `_usage` is never restored
anywhere — its only mutations are `_usage.add(message.usage)` at `TurnEnd`

sites (`session_commands.dart:26,131`). `_switchToMetadata` replays the
transcript but restores no usage, so after `/resume` or `/session <name>` the
ledger — and therefore the average's numerator — starts at zero, exactly like
`tok`/`turn`/cost.

The **behavior** is right (mirroring the footer's established
process-lifetime semantics is the consistent choice); the **comments** assert a
restore mechanism that does not exist and will mislead the next maintainer (and
made the ticket's E4 evidence claim unfounded). Please reword both doc comments
to say the meter mirrors `_usage`'s switch-reset semantics (everything —
window, factor, active time, settled denominator — re-zeroes on session
switch, and the average re-warms with the new session's first turn), or, if
session-lifetime was actually intended, restore the numerator on resume — but
then the denominator needs the same restore, or the first streamed second after
resuming a 50k-output-token session renders `avg 25000 t/s`.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the preset comment describes a replacement that never happened**

The comment (repeated in `tui_status_line_test.dart:180`) says *"the duplicated
trailing context-window label gives way to the live rate pair"* — but v0's
default preset right side was exactly `['session_name']` (origin/main

(`context_total` only existed in the `full`/`nerd` presets and the registry).

one"). Suggest rewording, e.g. *"gh-1762: the default band gains the live rate
pair after `session_name` — both render hidden without data, so an idle band
keeps its pre-gh-1762 width"* — the current wording sends a reader hunting for
a deleted `context_total` that was never in this preset.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `activeMsSettled` is public API with no production reader**

`int get activeMsSettled => _settledActiveMs;` is referenced only by tests (and
the doc prose). Everything else the meter exposes has a production consumer

The window decays through tool-execution gaps toward hidden (AC7); idle renders null, never `0 t/s` (the host gates on `isBusy`, the segment hides on null/zero). **The live rate renders on the band (the per-frame surface by design) and the snapshot seam.**

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

One subtle behavior in `calibrate`: `_settledActiveMs = _activeMs;` — the settle freezes the active time. But note `calibrate` is called at TurnEnd after `_usage.add(message.usage)`. Good.

Potential issues to consider:

1. `tokensPerSecondAvg` uses `_activeMs` (live denominator), while the snapshot reads `tokensPerSecondAvg(total.output)` — the band's average is live. During a new turn streaming, `_activeMs` grows while the ledger total stays constant (until TurnEnd adds usage). So the average will DECREASE during streaming until the turn settles. That's by design ("band's average stays live (per-frame by design)").

2. Division by zero: `spanMs` could be 0 → but checked by `_minSpanMs` floor. OK.

3. `_prune` uses `<=` cutoff; window boundary inclusive. Fine.

4. In `tokensPerSecond`, note the pruning at read time: if the read happens without new deltas (idle decay), it prunes and hides. Good.

5. `observeDelta` maps chars/4 * factor. `calibrate` multiplies `_factor * outputTokens / _messageTokens`. `_messageTokens` is the sum of the per-message estimated tokens (raw, before factor? No — `_count` already applies the factor: `_messageTokens += tokens` where tokens = chars/4*factor. So `_messageTokens` is factor-adjusted estimate. Then `_factor_new = _factor * outputTokens / _messageTokens`. If the true relation is tokens_true = chars/4 * factor_true, and message estimated with factor f: _messageTokens = chars/4*f. outputTokens is real. New factor = f * outputTokens / (chars/4 * f) = outputTokens / (chars/4). Correct — the factor converges to outputTokens/(chars/4). Good math.

7. Edge: `calibrate` sets `_messageTokens = 0` — so between calibrate and next startMessage, a stray endMessage would compute topUp = estimated - 0 = full message again. But endMessage is only called at message end, calibrate at turn end. If a turn has multiple assistant messages: startMessage, deltas, endMessage(est1); startMessage, deltas, endMessage(est2); turn end → calibrate(output). _messageTokens accumulates est1+est2 (both messages), and calibrate uses the total. void _onMessageUpdate(AssistantMessageEvent assistantMessageEvent) {

   _meter.startMessage();

 }
 _meter.endMessage(estimateTokens(message));
 _onAssistantMessageEnd(message);
}
``

Hmm — `if (start) { ...; return; }` then `_meter.endMessage(...)`. So endMessage is called on message END events (start=false). OK.
